blindSummary:
Trans visitors here face formal criminal exposure combined with a hostile social climate. A consolidated 2006 criminal-code statute criminalises sodomy (up to 1 year — a lighter formal penalty than neighbouring states carry, though open-ended indecency provisions add exposure), and an international human-rights organisation's 2024 report documents shrinking civic space threatening LGBT organising (the national LGBT organisation operates under pressure; its offices have been raided historically). There is no legal gender recognition, political rhetoric is hostile, and mob violence is documented — but prosecution under the sodomy law is rarer than in a neighbouring state, and a small organised community persists openly enough to litigate.

For a visitor: statutory exposure exists but enforcement is sporadic; social hostility is the main risk.
blindOutOfScope: Same-sex criminalisation is the vehicle; enforcement pattern is sporadic.
blindSourceSummaries: International legal-aid trust country profile: this country criminalises same-sex sexual activity between men and between women (sodomy, plus a supplementary offence of contact between males that a reasonable person would regard as indecent). (Only the opening of the profile was retrievable at fetch time.)

International human-rights organisation report (Jan 2024), with a title conveying an existential threat to local activists: escalating anti-LGBTI sentiment and the weaponisation of law across several countries in this world region — documenting a 2022/23 surge in fear, attacks and hostility here.

Opposition newspaper in exile (July 2018): the health ministry approved a training manual for all health practitioners on treating gay patients and sex workers in the country's health institutions - a practical step for inclusive healthcare despite criminalisation.

Academic social-work article (July 2012): gay people live secluded lives due to prejudice; the paper argues that homosexuality is indigenous to this country's culture and history, tracing same-sex relations across earlier and modern periods, and urges social workers to promote social justice for the gay community.
Academic journal article on homosexuality in this country (publisher platform; page largely navigation content at fetch time).

The national LGBT membership organisation's official site: a voluntary membership organisation established in 1990 - 4,000+ community members, 35 years of advocacy, 10 affinity groups, 4 resource centres; provides legal support (including for 'sodomy' arrests), counselling, hospital-fee assistance and empowerment programmes for local LGBTI people.
blindTangential: Sodomy criminalised (up to 1 year, sporadic enforcement) — formal exposure for visitors travelling with partners.
